facts.text: Patillas was founded in 1811 by Don Alejandro Ramírez, who named it after the nearby lagoon whose Taíno name means 'small stones'.
The Patillas Reservoir, created by the Carite Dam, supplies water to much of southeastern Puerto Rico and sits amid lush forests teeming with endemic birds.
San Benito Abad Church, a colonial‑era landmark in downtown Patillas, showcases classic Spanish architecture and has stood since the town’s early days.
Locals call Patillas 'La Esmeralda del Sur'—the Emerald of the South—thanks to its green hills, scenic beaches, and authentic coastal vibes.
Mountains rise within Patillas, with the Sierra de Cayey to the north and the Sierra de Guardarraya to the east shaping its rugged terrain.
Patillas Pueblo, the town’s downtown core, serves as the administrative center and hosts the historic heart of the municipality.
